top_cited_works.title: A simple model of mixing and chemical reaction in a turbulent shear layer
top_cited_works.abstract: Arguments are presented to show that the concept of gradient diffusion is inapplicable to mixing in turbulent shear layers. A new model is proposed for treating molecular mixing and chemical reaction in such flows at high Reynolds number. It is based upon the experimental observations that revealed the presence of coherent structures and that showed that fluid elements from the two streams are distributed unmixed throughout the layer by large-scale inviscid motions. The model incorporates features of the strained flame model and makes use of the Kolmogorov cascade in scales. Several model predictions differ markedly from those of diffusion models and suggest experiments for testing the two approaches.

top_cited_works.title: Structure, Penetration, and Mixing of Pulsed Jets in Crossflow
top_cited_works.abstract: Effects of periodic disturbances on the structure and mixing of a transverse jet have been investigated through chemically reactive laser-induced fluorescence experiments in a water model. Flow visualization experiments with a steady, round jet in crossflow revealed a distinct vortex loop merging pattern among the vortices that make up the curved shear layer around the jet. As the vortex loops are stretched and distorted, certain parts of the neighboring loops with the opposite or the same sign of vorticity merge, resulting in cancellation or intensification of the vorticity in the corresponding regions of the jet. When the flow rate of this jet was periodically modulated by a square wave, however, distinct vortex rings were created whose spacing and strength were dictated by the pulsing frequency for a given jet and crossflow combination. At low pulsing rates, these rings penetrated into the crossflow significantly deeper than the steady jet. An optimum pulsing frequency was found at which closely spaced vortex rings were observed, which penetrated as discrete vortices into the crossflow in the near field. recent_works.title: Spoiler-Integrated Micro-Wind-Turbine Array for Energy Harvesting
recent_works.abstract: Aircraft missions entail substantial losses of kinetic and potential energy, typically dissipated as heat or drag. Energy balance calculations for a typical airliner show that during the landing phase, drag devices experience the largest energy sink. In this study, we quantify these losses using energy balance equations and propose the integration of a micro wind turbine (MWT) array on the spoiler surfaces to recover a fraction of the wasted kinetic energy without degrading aerodynamic braking efficacy. The concept is evaluated experimentally assessing both aerodynamic performance and power recovery potential to find actual Cp and incremental drag with design selection of gearbox ratios, generator matching, airfoil blade selection, pitch control, and deployable door mechanisms. The experimental results indicate that the MWT operating at its designed tip speed ratio of 4, is capable of producing 9.04 W of power at a wind speed of 10 m/s. These findings demonstrate that spoiler mounted turbines can serve as a viable supplemental power source. Moreover, the results provide design guidelines that can inform future developments in aircraft energy harvesting technologies.

recent_works.title: Vortex Generator System for Enhancing Heat Transfer in Cryogenic Pipelines
recent_works.abstract: Limiting parasitic boil-off during the chilldown process is a major engineering challenge in cryogenic systems such as those present in propulsion systems, superconducting magnets, and liquified natural gas. With the majority of the boil-off occurring during the annular film boiling regime, significant consideration has been given to moderating the insulating effects of the vapor layer produced by the Leidenfrost Effect. In this paper, a novel method based on Vortex Generators (VGs) to disrupt the Leidenfrost vapor barrier, thereby enhancing heat transfer, accelerating chilldown, and limiting boil-off is proposed. Two mechanisms of heat transfer enhancement are discussed - surface rewetting and enhanced turbulent transport. In a low-mass flow experimental apparatus, the effectiveness of a set of VG configurations were tested and analyzed through visual comparison of outer wall temperature profiles and peak cooling times. Results indicate that the VG configurations produce improvements in heat transfer and reductions in chilldown times, with turbulent transport being the probable mechanism of action.

recent_works.title: Mixing in a Novel Rocket Engine
recent_works.abstract: A new rocket engine concept is proposed based on a transverse engine combustor. This transverse combustor design is modeled using CFD. In particular, DNS and LES are utilized to simulate reacting flows of fuel and oxidizer pairs. Conventional rocket engine designs incorporate an axial flow with many small nozzles. The proposed engine injects fluid propellent transverse to the dominant flow direction with two nozzles, one for each of the two reactants. Mixing is achieved with large, counter rotating vortices. This new configuration is anticipated to be less expensive to manufacture, lighter, and more reliable than existing designs.
